title: Montessori Geography — Houses Around the World 3-Part Cards (Uplands Media)

overview.description: Montessori 3-part nomenclature cards + control cards for houses/dwellings from around the world. Includes: Celtic Round House (Wales), Bungalow (North America), and more. Two font options (D'Nealian and Century Gothic) plus tracing fonts for writing practice. Designed for cardstock, lamination, and dry-erase marker reuse.
features: tracing font version for writing practice

dualFontOptions.description: Same cards available in D'Nealian and Century Gothic fonts. D'Nealian is common in US schools (slanted for cursive transition). Century Gothic is clean sans-serif. Teacher/parent picks whichever matches their handwriting curriculum.
dualFontOptions.value: Font choice is a real pain point for homeschoolers — different curricula use different handwriting styles. Offering both removes that friction.

tracingFontVersion.description: A third font version: tracing letters (dotted/dashed) so children can practice writing the vocabulary words. The nomenclature card becomes a writing practice tool too.
tracingFontVersion.value: Vocabulary learning + handwriting practice in one material. Multi-skill without adding pages.

geographyCulturalConnection.description: Each house type is labeled with both the house name AND the world region (Celtic Round House = Wales, Bungalow = North America). The child learns architecture + geography + cultural diversity simultaneously.
geographyCulturalConnection.value: Cross-curricular: architecture + geography + cultural awareness. 'Houses look different around the world' is an accessible entry to cultural diversity for young children.

notes: Third Montessori 3-part card set from Aless. Now applied to geography/cultural studies. The triple-font feature (D'Nealian + Century Gothic + tracing) is a new detail that the solar system and community helpers sets didn't have. This adds a writing practice dimension to the nomenclature card format. Total Montessori 3-part drops: astronomy + social studies + geography = 3 subjects, same format. The recipe is thoroughly validated.
